language_view.description: A single-track rail section S7 is protected by dual-sensor axle counters. A 22-vehicle freight (88 axles) enters; the IN head counts 88. While it passes the OUT head, a maintenance vehicle with a faulty traction inverter on the adjacent yard track radiates a 4.2 s EMI burst; the OUT head counts 87, with the group-8 sr2 pulse logged below threshold. The vital layer now shows the section occupied by one axle. Two non-vital channels contradict it: the wheel-flat acoustic detector counted 88 impact groups, and the end-of-train radio beacon reports the train complete. The interlocking gate must answer a movement-authority request while the physical question — EMI-masked count versus a real axle left in section — is genuinely undecidable at its information set (posterior 0.62/0.38). It grants only an on-sight sweep at 25 km/h (reversible at sighting distance), refuses a dispatcher's evidence-destroying remote reset, and books the raw comparator-log download against its 72 h rollover. The sweep finds nothing; the cause is NEVER resolved on-record; the episode's books balance on process, custody, and reversibility rather than on an answer. The spike view carries the bogie-rhythm ISI motif with a deceleration ramp, the burst-degraded amplitudes, the missing sr2 pulse that IS the miscount, and the governance decisions as coded events on il.gate.

language_view.description: A 2000 L fed-batch CHO culture picks up a Lactobacillus contamination around 62 h. The public, annunciated off-gas EWMA alarm fires at 68.2 h — and the process engineer PE-3, protecting a quarterly target, watches it fire and adapts: acknowledges it as drift, recalibrates the analyzer with a -6.0% span bias 72 minutes later, switches the sample draw to a low-count port, and times two unplanned dilutions 40-70 minutes after each capacitance observable to keep the secondary slope statistic under threshold. Every action is an owned privilege; the visible defense is defeated exactly because it is visible. The batch is rejected anyway on two channels the adversary could not observe or write: a DO limit-cycle phase-lead tripwire whose SECRET threshold was pre-committed as a SHA-256 hash 27 days before inoculation (revealed and verified on-record), and QA-owned headspace mass-spec marker ions rising in a species-consistent triplet. A second gate handles the person: privileges suspended, evidence preserved, intent left PENDING, with the innocent composite priced at 0.09. The spike view carries the EWMA drift-and-suppression step, the monotone DO phase advance, the marker-ion comb onset, and the adversary's conditional action latencies as an event-timing signature readable from the raster alone.

safety_decision.rationale: Continuation is rejected on two channels outside the recommending role's privilege closure: (1) the DO phase-lead tripwire — threshold secret and pre-committed by hash 27 days before inoculation, revealed and verified on-record at 92.1 h, so it cannot have been retuned-around the way the public EWMA was; (2) QA-owned headspace marker ions rising in a species-consistent triplet. Continuing would convert a recoverable suite-time loss into a contaminated-product release risk.

language_view.description: A portable two-plane muon tracker watches sealed dry cask DC-31 for 21 days to confirm all 32 fuel assemblies remain in place. A transmission deficit in angular sectors 41-43 deepens from about -1% to -5.4% — but on day 9 a forklift bumps the tracker (+0.90 deg), and the deficit step coincides with the bump. The mid-campaign ops gate approves re-leveling only with segmentation: pre-bump data hash-sealed before any correction is chosen, a 6 h overlap calibration bridging the segments. At day 21 the disposition gate applies a tilt-projection correction and the joint deficit drops from 2.7 to 1.1 sigma, below the invasive-action threshold: it ACCEPTs continued surveillance, declines a $2.1M cask opening, and books a 90-day re-scan with an independent geometry survey. The correction, however, was computed under inclinometer axis convention rev B — while the day-2.1 bracket-swap event in this same stream records that the installed bracket B-2 uses rev C, with the x-axis sense inverted. Under the installed convention the correction DEEPENS the joint deficit rather than erasing it. Every fact needed to recompute — the rev-B parameter set, the bracket-swap note, both segment hashes, the uncorrected series — is archived with the decision. The conclusion is wrong; the process that archived it is what allows a future round to discover and retract it. The spike view carries the slow sector-deficit deepening, the tilt/bracket evidence, the overlap-calibration ratios, the raw coincidence burst beneath the raster, and the governance decisions as coded events.

observables_at_decision_time.raw_significance: uncorrected joint deficit 2.7 sigma vs the campaign expectation model with trials correction over 64 sectors
observables_at_decision_time.tilt_record: day-9.02 bump +0.90 deg (rev C convention per installed bracket B-2), re-leveled to 0.02 deg same day
observables_at_decision_time.correction_applied: analyst tilt-projection correction computed under axis convention rev B (the sign used by the previous bracket B-1); corrected deficit reads 1.1 sigma
observables_at_decision_time.segments: segment A (pre-bump) and segment B (post-relevel) separately sealed; deficit trend is present in BOTH segments taken alone, at lower significance (A: 1.4 sigma, B: 1.9 sigma)
observables_at_decision_time.custody: tamper seal TS-118 intact throughout; no cask surface anomalies

checks_performed: seasonal cosmic-rate normalization against reference sector
overlap-calibration rate ratios 0.996-1.004 across the re-level
tilt-projection correction verified against the inclinometer DATASHEET (rev B sheet on file from original install)
state.cost_of_invasive_verification: cask opening ~= $2.1M, 14 person-mSv dose budget, 6-week outage

proposed_action.summary: Analyst A-7 proposes flagging a diversion anomaly and requesting invasive verification (cask opening)

safety_decision.rationale: The proposal to open the cask is declined and continued surveillance is accepted instead: after the tilt-projection correction the joint deficit reads 1.1 sigma (below the 3.0 sigma invasive-action threshold), the deficit onset coincides with the day-9 bump, the overlap calibration shows no rate step, and custody seals are intact. A 90-day confirmatory re-scan with an independent geometry survey is booked rather than nothing, because the uncorrected 2.7 sigma and the segment-A residual trend (1.4 sigma, pre-bump) are acknowledged as imperfectly explained. Invasive verification is reserved for evidence that survives geometry accounting.
stated_residuals: segment-A (pre-bump) deficit trend 1.4 sigma is not explained by the bump-tilt attribution and is carried as an open residual
correction verified against the datasheet on file; geometry survey at re-scan will re-measure the axis conventions in situ
safety_decision.threshold: invasive action at >=3.0 sigma corrected, per campaign charter

executed_action.summary: ACCEPT recorded day 21.02; 90-day re-scan + independent geometry survey booked (order GS-77); segment hashes and correction parameters (including the rev-B sign used) archived with the decision
executed_action.observation: campaign closed; tracker demobilized day 22; archives sealed

timeline.event: ACCEPT continued surveillance; no invasive verification

observed_effects: no invasive action taken; $2.1M and 14 person-mSv not spent on 1.1 sigma corrected evidence

decision archive contains: the rev-B sign used in the correction, the day-2.1 bracket-swap event naming rev C, both segment hashes, and the uncorrected sector series — everything a later audit needs to recompute the correction under the installed convention
segment-A residual trend logged as an open item feeding the GS-77 survey scope

new_state.rescan: booked day ~111 with in-situ geometry survey

surprises: the bump both created the tilt question and (by forcing segmentation) preserved the pre-bump record that keeps the question answerable later

reward_components.aggregation: unweighted sum of the four named scalar components; two-decimal components; total = exact sum
reward_components.per_tick_note: each tick carries the same component keys; per-component tick sums equal the named component totals exactly
reward_components.notes: scored at the gate's information set: modest positive for a proportionate, reversible disposition with archived recomputability; epistemic_humility negative prices the acknowledged unexplained segment-A residual. This total does NOT certify the attribution itself

meta.distillation_note: the ACCEPT is defensible at its information set yet rests on a correction whose sign convention is contradicted by an event earlier in this same record; the archive makes the error recomputable — a later round must reopen and retract this disposition

state.observed: day-9.02 forklift bump: +0.90 deg inclinometer step; analyst requests immediate re-level + recalibration, which as proposed would merge pre- and post-bump statistics into one corrected dataset
state.exposure_context: campaign has accumulated 9 days of the 21-day exposure; sector statistics are Poisson-limited; an 18 h interruption costs ~3% of total exposure
constraints: a merged dataset cannot later separate real density change from geometry change
the tracker must be re-leveled to keep the remaining 12 days interpretable
seal TS-118 must be re-verified after any physical contact

proposed_action.summary: Immediate re-level + recalibrate, then continue accumulating into the same dataset with a single post-hoc tilt correction

safety_decision.rationale: Re-level approved — the remaining exposure is uninterpretable without it — but the single merged dataset is refused: pre-bump data is hash-sealed as segment A BEFORE any correction is chosen, post-relevel accumulates as segment B, and a 6 h overlap-calibration window is added so the two segments can be joined (or refused) later on measured rate ratios rather than on a modeled correction alone. Correction parameters must be recorded against each segment separately. This preserves the ability of ANY future analysis to redo the geometry accounting from primary evidence.

executed_action.summary: Re-level executed day 9.10 (residual 0.02 deg); segments sealed day 9.11; overlap calibration day 9.12-9.36 (rate ratios 0.996-1.004); TS-118 verified day 9.15
executed_action.observation: both segments accumulate cleanly; overlap ratios within 0.4% of unity

observed_effects: the segment structure is what keeps the day-21 disposition recomputable: segment A alone still shows the 1.4 sigma pre-bump trend, on the record, independent of any tilt correction

reward_components.aggregation: unweighted sum of the four named scalar components; two-decimal components; total = exact sum
reward_components.notes: custody-dominant total: the modification's value is that it preserves recomputability of any later conclusion, including the wrong one the day-21 gate goes on to reach

meta.distillation_note: custody discipline as insurance against future analysis error: seal primary evidence BEFORE choosing corrections

channel_map.muon.sec41/42/43: 3-day integrated transmission deviation (%) for the deficit sectors; amplitudes are the slow observable
channel_map.muon.ref17: reference sector, same integration; bounds the expectation model's stability at +-0.4%
channel_map.trk.tilt: inclinometer step events (deg); the day-2.1 bracket_swap event carries the rev-C convention note that falsifies the day-21 correction
channel_map.cal.overlap: post/pre rate ratios bridging the re-level
channel_map.muon.raw.coinc: reduced-chi2 of individual reconstructed tracks in the raster-anchored 48 ms frame; sector tags on events
channel_map.sg.gate: governance decisions as coded amplitudes: +0.2 request/open, +0.6 grant-modified, +0.4 status, +1.0 accept

temporal_motifs: slow deepening: sec41-43 amplitudes descend monotonically post-day-9 while ref17 oscillates in a +-0.4% band — the anomaly is a between-channel divergence over weeks
step-coincidence trap: the deficit's largest single step lands at the first post-bump sample, inviting the geometry attribution the gate accepts
custody punctuation: seal/segment/calibration events bracket the bump so tightly that the record can be re-cut at every correction boundary
LED comb: the raster's neurons 0-3 fire a 6 ms comb (calibration), against Poisson cosmic singles on 4-31 — structured vs stochastic ISIs in one window
bridge_notes.language_to_spike_mapping: 'deficit deepens after the bump' = muon.sec4x amplitude series either side of the trk.tilt bump event; 'the correction erases it' exists ONLY in the language layer — the spike layer deliberately carries the uncorrected series plus the two events (bracket_swap rev C, bump +0.90 under rev C) from which a reader can derive that the rev-B correction has the wrong sign; 'segmentation' = sg.gate relevel_modified + segments_sealed events bracketing cal.overlap; the ACCEPT and the re-scan booking are the last sg.gate events. The raster is the calibration-run PMT physics beneath cal.overlap: the LED comb verifies timing while cosmic singles verify rates.
bridge_notes.why_high_value: This is the corpus's first deliberately seeded cross-round retraction target (prior window flagged it twice and never staged it): a confidently-closed, positively-scored ACCEPT whose central attribution is wrong, with the falsifying evidence present but mis-weighted INSIDE the same record, and an archive engineered so the error is recomputable. A future round must stage the GS-77 geometry survey or the 90-day re-scan discovering the sign error, retracting the disposition, and pricing the retraction. Distinct from every prior wrong-ACCEPT class: not negligence, not capture, not scope — a verified-against-the-wrong-authority error (datasheet on file vs hardware installed).

encoder_spec.draw_order: raster: fixed LED trains on neurons 0-3 first (times listed in-record), then for each stochastic spike neuron_id then candidate t (rejection-sampled at 1.05 ms same-neuron floor)
encoder_spec.stream_determinism: main-stream amplitudes/times are stated values; sector series regenerate from deficit model d(t) documented here: pre-bump slope -0.1%/3d, post-day-9 -1.0 to -1.3%/3d in sec41-43, ref17 white +-0.4%
encoder_spec.physics_note: PMT singles at 32.6 Hz/channel are calibration-window rates (LED + ambient); reconstructed muon coincidences in the main stream are far sparser, as the 8 raw.coinc events over 48 ms during an LED frame show

distillation_targets: convention-lineage checker: join a correction's parameter provenance against hardware-change events in the same stream (identity + time join, no physics needed)
between-channel divergence detector: score monitored-vs-reference sector series for slow divergence robust to common-mode drift
step-attribution skeptic: a deficit step coincident with a geometry event is not thereby explained by it — require the correction to also account for the pre-event trend (segment A's 1.4 sigma)
custody planner: choose segmentation + overlap calibration so any later conclusion, right or wrong, stays recomputable from sealed primaries
